hints: Look closely at the word prophase. What do chromosomes look like at this stage, single threads or X-shaped structures made of two sister chromatids?
Remember each single chromatid has two ends, so two telomeres. How many ends does one X-shaped prophase chromosome have in total?
walkthrough:
**Recall what a telomere is**

Think of a telomere as a protective cap on the end of a chromatid. Every chromatid has two ends, so one chromatid always has 2 telomeres.

**Remember what prophase means for chromosome structure**

Prophase is after DNA replication in S phase. So each of the 32 chromosomes is now made of two sister chromatids joined together, looking like an X.

That means per chromosome:
$$2 \text{ chromatids} \times 2 \text{ telomeres per chromatid} = 4 \text{ telomeres}$$

**Do the final count**

Now just multiply up for the whole cell:
$$32 \text{ chromosomes} \times 4 \text{ telomeres} = 128 \text{ telomeres}$$
That matches option D, well done.

options.A: This counts only 1 telomere per chromosome. Each chromosome has two ends, and in prophase it has two chromatids, so this is far too low.
options.B: This counts 2 telomeres per chromosome. That would be correct for unreplicated chromosomes in G1, but not for replicated prophase chromosomes with two chromatids.
options.C: There is no biological basis for 3 telomeres per chromosome. Each chromatid must have an even number of ends, so this value is impossible.
options.D: Correct. In prophase each of the 32 chromosomes has 2 chromatids x 2 telomeres = 4 telomeres, giving 128 in total.
